interpretation.warmClean: Two concurrent discovery commands (diff-files + ls-files --others) plus write-tree. No per-file JS work. 27ms at 10k, 84ms at 50k, 159ms at 100k.
interpretation.warm1Dirty: Dominated by `git diff-files`'s O(N) stat walk over the shadow index. The shadow index resolves via alternates to the source's objects. This is the cost the reviewer predicted (the OpenCode-style algorithm is still O(N) at the git layer for authoritative dirty detection). At 100k the stat walk dominates; at 10k the candidate-only staging is the main cost.
interpretation.followUp: The reviewer named the follow-up investigations: Git fsmonitor, untracked cache behavior, split index, platform filesystem behavior. `core.fsmonitor=false` is set explicitly (matching OpenCode's design). `core.untrackedCache=true` is now set on the shadow; it warms across captures in production (the benchmark recreates the shadow each run, so the cache does not help there). The warm-clean path is the steady state for an idle developer reading code; the warm-1-dirty path is what a Send after an edit costs.
